Third-party source provenance
Recorded 2026-11-08

This directory contains unchanged reference snapshots used to build and extend
the teaching examples in this textbook. It does not contain a CVX distribution
or any bundled optimization solver. Upstream notices in the files are retained.
No new license is assigned here to the user-facing textbook or its newly written
content. The original licenses apply to the corresponding upstream files only.

1. CVX example library
Repository: https://github.com/cvxr/CVX
Commit: a0a775908bc1eec1625d56498d0224132b0d8b7f

Local paths are the same as their upstream paths under the CVX/ prefix:
  CVX/LICENSE.txt
  CVX/examples/antenna_array_design/ant_array_min_sidelobe.m
  CVX/examples/gp_tutorial/power_control.m

The upstream LICENSE.txt explicitly places the examples/ library in the public
domain and requests appropriate credit. This statement is separate from the
license of CVX itself and of any solvers. The full upstream license document is
included as evidence; only the named example files are redistributed here.

The two examples were written for CVX by Almir Mutapcic on 2006-02-02 and
2006-02-08, respectively. Their headers credit Stephen Boyd and the cited
antenna-array and geometric-programming publications. These snapshots have not
been edited or run as part of textbook validation.

2. CVXPY example notebooks
Repository: https://github.com/cvxpy/examples
Commit: 73a6892ef5bea4ded68f8f9fab17e48119dc62f5
License: Apache License 2.0, full text in cvxpy-examples/LICENSE

Local paths are the same as their upstream paths under the cvxpy-examples/ prefix:
  cvxpy-examples/LICENSE
  cvxpy-examples/notebooks/WWW/water_filling_BVex5.2.ipynb
  cvxpy-examples/notebooks/WWW/maximise_minimum_SINR_BV4.20.ipynb

The notebooks credit Robert Gowers, Roger Hill, Sami Al-Izzi, Timothy Pollington,
and Keith Briggs. They identify their mathematical examples as Boyd and
Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, Example 5.2 and Exercise 4.20. The snapshots
here are unchanged. The Apache license and original notebook attribution have
been retained. No upstream NOTICE file was present in the repository root at
the recorded version; this file records the source attribution for this package.

Changes in the new textbook examples, relative to those source examples:
  - New problem data and independent residual checks are used.
  - Water filling is written as log2(1+p/alpha) so that the sum rate in bit/s for four 1-Hz subchannels (and the
    conversion to aggregate spectral efficiency) is explicit, rather than
    using a natural logarithm with an additive constant.
  - Power and SINR constraints are expressed directly in the stated physical
    units; any group constraint is a total-power constraint as written, rather
    than an implicitly normalized average.
  - The array example uses an explicitly specified uniform linear array and
    explains why a finer angle grid is needed to detect sampling error.
    No new array-design numerical experiment or upstream MATLAB run is claimed.
  - New derivations explain mathematical structure, solver choice, assumptions,
    stopping rules, and what numerical evidence can establish.
These adaptations appear in the textbook chapters and new experiment programs,
not in the unchanged upstream snapshots under this directory.

3. User-specified mathematical research-writing rules
Source: https://github.com/hongjinrui/writing_skills/blob/main/SKILL.md
Read date: 2026-11-08
Local snapshot: writing_rules/SKILL.md
License: MIT, full license and attribution retained inside that file.
The snapshot credits hongjinrui, JiahaoLi-creator, and Kiterlin. It is included
to identify the exact writing guidance followed; the textbook does not claim
that those authors reviewed or endorsed its mathematical content.

4. Additional references
The textbook cites standard books and research papers for mathematical results.
Those books and papers are not redistributed in this package. New Chinese
exposition, the problem-family organization, derivations, exercises, and plots
are prepared for the present textbook. A publicly readable PDF is not treated
as an open license to reproduce its text, diagrams, or source files.
